problems.problem: The regenerated scene inserted four literal aubergines (eggplants) with green calyxes plus a pile of shredded紫色 vegetable matter across the bottom band (y≈1200-1440), directly under and beside the 'EAU DE PARFUM' line. The concept's 'pooled pile' was meant as settled velvet nap, not produce; these generated props read as a grocery still-life, contradict the luxury velvet concept and clash with the clean staged surfaces of references 3 and 5. No studio equipment is visible, but the props are worse interference.

The subtitle 'EAU DE PARFUM' at y=1284-1299 is set inside the debris field: white confetti flecks and an eggplant silhouette sit behind and between its letters (visible at x≈420-660), destroying legibility and the quiet plaque band. The title's descender zone also grazes the top of the debris pile. Ink contrast itself is fine; the fault is the busy generated matter behind the smallest type.

The new velvet ledge does seat the flacon (base y=1008 rests on the raised tabletop, not floating), but the ledge's bright front-facing sheen band runs straight behind the lower body at the same value as the cap highlights, and the eggplant cluster at bottom-left/right outweighs the plaque band, so the eye exits the poster through the props instead of resting on the name line.

The theatrical 'curtain call' concept (velvet house curtain, calm plaque band, single gold spark) is broken: the vegetable props introduce a second, incompatible narrative and a second material family (wet glossy produce vs dry velvet), so material, palette and copy no longer express one idea.
